releases.title: A clearer first launch
releases.summary: A small follow-up to the first public release, with clearer update results and the optional support invitation.
changes: Checking for updates keeps the correct up-to-date or compatibility result after Sparkle's normal no-update alert closes. A completed check no longer becomes a misleading failure in Help or App Logs.
About uses release-neutral wording beneath the exact version and build. The first public 0.1.0 remains available unchanged.

The optional Support Traverse invitation now uses the existing direct-shipping edition identity. It waits until the second launch, stays out of setup and active work, remembers each released update and respects the reminder preference. Support remains available in Help; every feature stays free.

releases.title: Meet Traverse
releases.summary: Your files, side by side. The first public release brings local folders, servers, archives, editing and storage tools into one native Mac workspace.
changes: The direct Developer ID edition uses normal macOS user access instead of App Sandbox grants. Privacy prompts, file permissions, protected system locations and existing operation integrity checks still apply. It keeps its own data and update feed; unfinished work in an earlier edition must be completed there.

Crash reports stay on this Mac. Help offers an editable report, optional current CPU and memory details, private-detail hiding and a prefilled GitHub issue draft. You decide whether to share or publish it. Original native captures stay local; nothing is submitted automatically.

Hide the sidebar from View or its native divider, and reopen it from the footer. Its width, expanded branches and position are preserved. Source, Discord and voluntary support links live in Help, with a second-launch invitation and an update-reminder opt-out.
Traverse is free and open source under GNU GPLv3. Help includes the complete license and a voluntary Support Traverse page; development support never unlocks or limits application features.

Compress to ZIP immediately or extract an archive into its own named folder. Compress… and Extract… keep the full options available. Existing names are preserved and successful operations support Undo.

New Folder creates immediately and lets you rename in place. Move to Trash also starts directly, with an optional confirmation in Operations settings. Open Folder offers remembered access so supported later operations need fewer repeated folder choices.

Move files and folders to the Mac’s Trash, Undo after reopening Traverse, or restore a recorded group from Traverse Trash. Existing names and changed items are checked before restoration; earlier unresolved attempts remain protected.

Create ZIP and TAR archives from local files and folders while keeping originals unchanged. ZIPs also support file and folder creation, Add and Paste, Rename, Remove, Duplicate, grouping and supported text editing with recoverable original updates or a separate copy.

Browse ZIP, TAR and prepared compressed TAR folders with editable addresses, Back and Forward, member Properties, Copy Path and inline previews. Supported archive copies, extraction and ZIP drag-out retain checked delivery and Undo after reopening Traverse.

Download files, selected groups and folders from SFTP and SMB to a chosen Mac folder or another Traverse pane. Existing names stay protected and completed copies support Undo after reopening Traverse.

Server Rename, Move, Cut/Paste and Upload share the ordinary browser flows. File and folder uploads support drag and Paste; regular-file Copy and Duplicate stay within the same connection or share. SMB selections allow up to 64 roots within 1 GiB.

Edit supported text on SFTP and encrypted SMB connections. Changed server files are protected from stale Saves, with direct Before Save and Edited Text review for a changed-file refusal, plus offline saved versions. OpenSSH user certificates can refresh before a remembered reconnect.

Traverse Editor adds richer syntax colours and per-type opening choices, JSON with Comments formatting, smarter indentation and Backspace, and adjustable Find colours. Editor Defaults keeps optional behaviour controls together. Redo preserves the caret inside the indentation it restores, so the next keystroke stays in the expected place.

Saved Versions can remove fresh local editor copies through macOS Trash after confirmation, keeping the original document unchanged. Removing those saved copies ends their Undo; older unresolved records stay protected.

Supported drive-health readings use a dedicated read-only service in the direct-distribution app. Optional Live monitoring is explicitly enabled for internal drives; older saved preferences do not enable it automatically. Unsupported devices remain clearly labelled, and dated readings stay distinct from current results.

Open Benchmark directly from the selected device in Drives. Benchmarks stay tied to that drive and expose dated summaries or JSON reports without private folder paths or drive identifiers. Stop, device changes and closing retain active-work cleanup.

Storage Analysis reuses recorded results across sessions and can refresh changed folders. Selected cleanup reuses the guarded file/folder Trash and Undo flow. Properties shows the analyzed location and timing, and startup-drive analysis offers a separate Data-volume choice when needed.

Server Find includes names beyond the visible row cache, with clearer incomplete-listing feedback. Server Properties can calculate a dated folder total without downloading file contents, and reuse a matching observed measurement.

Improved responsive columns, shared window presentation and drive transitions, readable enlarged settings, saved-server feedback and clearer operation results keep common flows consistent. Confirmed archive actions now say Completed in Recovery, just like other successful operations. The Open in Traverse folder Service opens selected Finder folders without changing the default folder app.

Properties keeps a dated storage summary after Full Analysis closes and reopens that result in one click. Drives shows actions relevant to the current page, with an explicit Off state when live health readings are unavailable.
Connection details use clearer native headings, the current folder and dated observations. Short footers stay compact, with the detailed context available on hover.

File is easier to scan: tab controls, archive actions, transfer tools and operation details have compact native submenus. Everyday actions and their keyboard shortcuts remain available, including direct sharing and Copy Path in file context menus.

Changing interface size crossfades the real layout without replacing controls or losing keyboard focus. Shared tool windows use a gentler closing fade, with Reduced, Off and system Reduce Motion preferences respected.

releases.title: Everyday work, made smoother
releases.summary: A private beta update for more dependable file operations, native text editing and clearer storage insight.
changes: Copy, Duplicate, Move and Rename retain clearer Results and guarded Undo. Traverse’s Move to Trash and earlier Trash Undo or recovery actions are temporarily unavailable in this restricted beta while macOS file protection is qualified. Existing history remains visible; use Finder for Trash.
Supported text files open in Traverse Editor by default. Choose Traverse, the macOS default or another app separately for each supported file type in Settings.

The native editor adds document tabs, richer syntax colours, blue Find highlights, Replace and Undo, Go to Line, JSON formatting, comments and line tools. JSON brackets can complete automatically and Return indents a new block; separate preferences control these conveniences.
Clear extensionless JSON, HTML, XML and script headers can select the editor language automatically. Manual language choices and opt-out take priority, and filenames stay as chosen.
Edit supported text directly on a normal SFTP connection. Save checks for external changes and retains before/edited versions for local review after disconnecting.

Upload a new file, folder or a small selection of up to three items to an SMB share through Upload or drag and drop. Existing destination names stay protected. SMB Paste, server actions and server-to-Mac copies remain unavailable in this beta.
Improved server connection compatibility when private beta updates are enabled.
Saved servers remain visible offline in the sidebar and This Mac. Reconnect uses available saved sign-in details and verified identity, while missing information still opens its normal review.

Saved storage analyses reopen across sessions. Refresh can check changed folders and reuse dated observations; Scan Every Folder always checks everything, and uncertain change history falls back to a complete scan.

Properties and Storage Analysis show File size and Size on disk together when available, alongside the scanned location, observation dates and scan duration. Size on disk can differ for sparse, compressed and shared storage.
Refresh automatically waits for earlier analysis readers to finish. The latest request runs, while Stop or closing the window can cancel a waiting request.
Filenames keep priority as split panes get narrower. Explicitly resized columns are respected, and enlarged interface sizes retain readable Name columns.

Settings, Help and tool windows share more consistent navigation, spacing, glass surfaces and optional closing motion. Chart hover and keyboard transitions are more subtle, with Full, Reduced and Off choices.
Operation Results can open the matching App Logs trace, even after another command has run. Logs stay on this Mac and exclude filenames, paths, document contents, search text and passwords.
Explorer Control-key selection and shortcuts, consistent rectangle selection, clearer sharing commands and per-file opening indicators improve everyday browsing.

This restricted beta keeps binary server Downloads, in-app archive extraction, ZIP member changes and Traverse Trash actions unavailable while their protection checks are completed. ZIP browsing, text previews and creating ZIPs from eligible local files remain available. Additional server actions and the Trash manager remain in local Preview.

releases.title: A clearer, more comfortable Traverse
releases.summary: Improved everyday browsing, setup, storage insights and beta support tools.
changes: Improved Copy, Move and Undo handling for downloaded files and macOS security metadata.
Choose Folder Access is available when a file operation is denied, without retrying a change automatically.
Help brings together detailed App Logs, version history, About and direct links to support and feedback.
Inspect correlated commands, queue/access state, worker stages and native error codes; pause, clear or export local logs without file names, paths, passwords or file contents.
Private beta update checks use your invitation password, with optional Keychain saving; review the changes before downloading and installing.
More memory-efficient recursive filename search, with clear incomplete and unavailable results.
Largest Files and clearer storage details help explain recorded analysis.
App Logs keeps export and navigation controls visible in a compact Help window.
New tabs start at This Mac; choose Home or the current folder in Settings. Duplicate Tab keeps its separate purpose.
Choose and remember access for each drive from a clearer setup checklist. Apple’s folder picker confirms each selection.
Enlarge text and controls from 100% to 150%, with a live preview in Settings and setup that adapts to the available width.
Subtler folder and This Mac transitions, consistent Glass tool-window headers and clearer Places and Pinned Folders.
Accordion headings expand or collapse when you click their names, as well as their chevrons.
Storage charts use richer colors, reflected lighting and dimensional edges. Projects open a category breakdown with recorded folders available separately.
Update restarts can restore local tabs, panes and supported tool windows without changing your normal startup choice.
More tool windows support resizing, with scrolling to keep controls reachable at larger text sizes.
Setup groups startup, familiar navigation, search, access and private beta updates into clear steps. New users reopen their last tabs and panes by default; existing startup choices stay unchanged.
Permissions has its own Settings page, with remembered drives, a draggable Traverse icon for Full Disk Access and an explicit local-network request. macOS remains in control of permission approval.

releases.title: Remember your places
releases.summary: Simpler setup and remembered folder or drive access.
changes: Setup remembers selected folder access by default; you can change that choice.
Review remembered locations, choose them again or forget them from Settings.
An optional short tour introduces navigation, file work and storage analysis.
A clearer drag-to-Applications installer and improved access explanations.

releases.title: A more welcoming start
releases.summary: First-run choices and clearer ways to choose folder access.
changes: Choose Glass or Solid, motion and familiar Mac or Explorer workflows during setup.
Review which features use selected folders, optional protected-data access and network permissions.
Improved startup-drive discovery, This Mac transitions and the shortcut search field.

releases.title: The first private beta
releases.summary: Traverse brings browsing, organisation and useful file tools together.
changes: Independent tabs and panes, saved launch profiles and familiar file navigation.
Guarded local file operations, operation results, Undo and recovery review.
ZIP browsing, checking, extraction and creation within the supported beta formats.
Metadata-only storage analysis, private names and labels, and read-only SMB/SFTP browsing.
